module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Finite

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The cycle rank of `G` (or cyclomatic number) is the minimum number of edges
    that must be removed to eliminate all cycles. -/
noncomputable def cycleRank (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  G.edgeFinset.card + Fintype.card G.ConnectedComponent - Fintype.card α

end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: The definition uses the closed formula |E| + c − |V| in ℕ rather than explicitly minimizing the number of edges deleted to eliminate all cycles.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let n, m, c be the vertex, edge, and connected-component counts. A spanning forest has n−c edges, so deleting its complement eliminates all cycles using m−n+c deletions. Conversely, any cycle-breaking deletion leaves a spanning forest with c′ ≥ c components and n−c′ ≤ n−c edges, requiring at least m−n+c deletions. Thus the minimum is exactly m+c−n. Spanning-forest existence also gives m+c ≥ n, so Lean's natural-number subtraction does not truncate a negative value. Mathlib counts unordered edges once and includes isolated vertices as components. The argument includes the empty graph.

review.notes: Reviewed the file's sole declaration. No direct uses were found in either problem files or other reusable definitions; only the umbrella-module import references this module. No duplicate or conflicting Mathlib definition was found. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully without sorry. It proves cycle rank zero for all finite edgeless graphs, all finite trees, and graphs on subsingleton vertex types; it also proves the minimum-deletion characterization for edgeless graphs. Computational checks give ranks 0,0,0,1,3 for K₀ through K₄, rank 1 for a triangle plus an isolated vertex, and rank 0 for one edge plus two isolated vertices. The general minimum-deletion equivalence above was checked mathematically, not fully formalized in Lean.
